evidence: FAIL (one observable owned by two functional criteria). tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:290 (cw_last_good_recovery, weight 2.0): "run a draft with an endless loop that the app ends at its time limit ... A later valid Run must work normally. Fails if ... a later valid Run does not work." tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:299 (cw_time_limit_recovery, weight 1.5): "run a draft with an endless loop written in the source ... a final valid Run must show its own new output ... Fails if ... the final valid Run does not work." Both grade the single public sentence in environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5 "The workspace must accept a later valid Run" in the same situation (a valid Run after a run ended at the time limit). Line 299 disowns the restored picture ("Whether the earlier picture returns to the preview is scored elsewhere, not here") but neither criterion disowns the later Run, unlike every other shared observable in this file (stop reason, time-limit reason, both modifier clicks, conflict message, repeated restore all carry a 'scored elsewhere, not here' sentence). NOTES (not defects under this row). (1) No contradictory pair found: checked Tab-indent vs keyboard exit (functional:74 vs polish:23), one-step vs repeated Undo (functional:29/128/398 vs ui.md:9), restore refused-or-appended vs repeat-safe replay (functional:371 vs 380), last-good restore vs stop/supersede marker suppression (290 vs 308/317), console retention (218 vs 254), desktop vs 390px layout (visual:40 vs polish:68), token colouring vs readability (functional:173 vs visual:24); a single app can satisfy all of them. (2) Control-fact reuse that I accept under qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md ('refusing a stale save and preserving the dirty editor are different outcomes'; 'Reuse an observed fact, not another row's pass flag'): cw_stale_save_keeps_draft re-observes the unchanged record of cw_stale_save_refused (353/362), cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state re-observes the live library update of cw_live_library_update (389/398), cw_restore_request_repeat_safe re-observes restore-adds-a-revision of cw_history_restore_retry (371/380). Each is a necessary positive control (the dead feature would otherwise pass by doing nothing), but one root defect costs 3.0, 3.5 and 2.0 of 59.0 functional weight respectively. (3) tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:32 cw_shared_saved_record (save, clear browser storage, reload, exact title/filename/source) is repeated as the first half of functional:344 cw_save_reload_restart. Zero-weight gate vs scored criterion, so no double credit; redundant judge work only. (4) functional:344 "Fails if the marker could not be typed inside the first line" makes arrow-key caret movement, owned by cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers (functional:38), a fail condition of the persistence criterion; fixture-feasibility coupling, low impact. (5) The id cw_history_restore_retry (functional:366) no longer grades a retry ("What happens when the same restore request is sent twice is scored elsewhere, not here"); stale name, could mislead a judge. (6) Evidence: none of the 22 artifacts in raw-evidence-index.json exists on disk (qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/ holds only results/build.log and results/restart.log, directory mtime 20:27; the hosted-run folders hold only *.log), so hashes are unverified and no run exercises this row. Done well: single-owner sentences are used consistently, Polish and Visual prompts and criteria explicitly hand correctness to other dimensions, and the three Visual criteria are scoped apart from each other.
counterexample: An app that ends an endless loop at five seconds, shows the time-limit reason and restores the last-good picture, but leaves that static picture covering the preview so the next valid Run's output is not shown (or does not rebuild its runner after the timeout). That one defect is a stated fail condition of both cw_time_limit_recovery (1.5) and cw_last_good_recovery (2.0): 3.5 of 59.0 functional weight for one public sentence, even though the app's picture restore after error, Stop and time limit all work.
suggested_fix: Give the post-time-limit Run one owner: keep it in cw_time_limit_recovery and reword cw_last_good_recovery so its later valid Run is checked after the error and after Stop only, adding 'Whether Run works again after a time limit is scored elsewhere, not here' (or the reverse), then re-freeze.
